title: cosettling
description: The cosettling T^{-1}(w) of a state w is the set of presheaves whose forward closure T produces w in one step - the backward-dynamics counterpart to the settling closure operator. It is generated by inverting one step of settling, and is multi-valued: many presheaves typically close to the same w.

state.description: the target state w in KP(B) whose one-step pre-images this object collects

preimages.description: { v in KP(B) : T(v) = w }, the single-step pre-images of w under the settling closure operator T

multiValued.description: cosettling is not a clean inverse to T: multiple presheaves close to the same w, so T^{-1}(w) is set-valued

containment.description: for closure-active w (T(w)=w), every v in T^{-1}(w) satisfies v subseteq w, by inflation

maximum.description: w itself lies in T^{-1}(w) and is the top of T^{-1}(w) under subseteq

closedUnderUnion.description: if v, v' in T^{-1}(w) then v cup v' in T^{-1}(w); so T^{-1}(w) is a finite join-subsemilattice with top of [bot, w]

hasMinimum.description: no minimum in general - distinct minimal pre-images are typically incomparable, and T^{-1}(w) is not closed under intersection
